paths.description: Entry page and primary navigation, including the automatic important-notice modal; represents the public landing template.
Primary farmer registration, e-token and login form; represents the highest-risk transactional journey.
Fertilizer tracking/status surface; represents lookup and service-state messaging.
About Us page; represents the long-form content template.
Privacy policy; represents policy and trust content.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the system color scheme.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the dark probe still measured the body as rgb(255,255,255) with rgb(33,37,41) text, and the screenshot remained light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and derive surfaces, text, controls and imagery from light/dark tokens; use light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.summary: Most continuous animation remains active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found six of seven animations still running, including ripple, aiGlow, slideroll and slide; only the scroll animation paused.
findings.suggestedFix: In prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove non-essential animation and use short opacity-only state changes where feedback is needed.

findings.summary: No high-contrast adaptation is evident.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no contrast preference or forced-colors adaptation, while the site relies on pale green/orange decorative treatments.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast styles that retain boundaries, focus indicators and readable text.

findings.summary: Primary route changes have no continuity.
findings.evidence: The inspected MPA pages use ordinary navigation and DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a no-motion fallback for stable shared page elements.

findings.summary: Animations are timer-driven rather than scroll/state-driven.
findings.evidence: The animation probe found long-running CSS animations (3–15 seconds), but no authored animation-timeline usage was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Tie any motion that communicates scroll progress to scroll timelines; remove decorative perpetual motion.

findings.summary: Interactive cards and media do not provide natural direct-manipulation feedback.
findings.evidence: Visual and DOM inspection found click handlers and generic Bootstrap animation, but no snap, gesture, overscroll or physics-based interaction on the card-heavy landing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use direct-manipulation patterns only where they improve the task, with accessible button alternatives and reduced-motion support.

findings.summary: Long mobile pages provide weak progress and continuation cues.
findings.evidence: The mobile landing page is 4,315 CSS pixels tall, while the screenshot shows a full-height modal and no page progress or clear continuation cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose scrollability and current location with a restrained sticky header, progress cue, or section navigation.

findings.summary: Attention is captured by an automatic notice instead of guided toward the primary service.
findings.evidence: Both desktop and mobile first views are blocked by a large modal before the user can see or choose the main registration and tracking tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Put the short service notice inline near the relevant action and let the primary task remain visible; reserve modal interruption for urgent, time-critical blocking information.

findings.summary: An unsolicited modal blocks all landing-page content on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: The first screenshot at both viewport sizes shows a modal and backdrop covering the page; the notice is lengthy and not tied to a user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the automatic modal with an inline, dismissible notice that remembers dismissal and does not block navigation.

findings.summary: The notice dialog is unnamed and implemented as a generic role-based container.
findings.evidence: The semantic probe found the visible role=dialog had neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby; Lighthouse also failed aria-dialog-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog (or fully conforming modal pattern), label it from its heading, manage focus, and provide Esc and light-dismiss behavior where appropriate.

findings.summary: Competing decorative chrome obscures the core services.
findings.evidence: The clear-page and crawler screenshots show banners, portraits, ticker, video control, floating accessibility control and multiple card treatments before core tasks; the automatic modal adds another layer.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce decorative bands and duplicated visual treatments; establish one compact service-first hierarchy.

findings.summary: Responsiveness is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero stylesheets containing @container; the same card/form components are tightly coupled to page-width utility classes such as w-50.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries for reusable cards and forms so they adapt to their allocated space, not only the viewport.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are below recommended touch size and field labeling is fragile.
findings.evidence: The form probes found 19–23px-high links/radios and many controls without programmatic labels; focus was visible, but target size remains small.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24×24 CSS pixel targets (prefer 44×44 for primary touch controls), preserve focus-visible styling and attach explicit labels.

findings.summary: The landing page hides its primary purpose and actions behind a notice.
findings.evidence: At first load, the registration and tracking actions are outside the visible interaction layer because the automatic notice occupies the viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Lead with two clearly named primary tasks and place service status as compact supporting information.

findings.summary: The primary identity flow uses duplicate IDs, inaccessible controls and blocked paste.
findings.evidence: The registration DOM contains duplicate id values (OtpType, aadharNo, chk_OTP), 14 unlabeled controls, and onpaste handlers on Aadhaar inputs, undermining reliable completion and assistive technology.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a unique ID and explicit label, allow paste, use inputmode/numeric constraints without blocking assistive input, and test the end-to-end OTP states.

findings.summary: Service and validation states lack robust recovery semantics.
findings.evidence: The tracking page reports that home delivery is unavailable as static body copy, and the primary form controls lack the labeling/error associations needed for actionable validation recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Use role=status for service state, associate validation messages with fields, focus the first invalid field, and provide a clear retry or alternate channel.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.4s, FCP 4.3s and TTI 9.5s (performance 0.63); the local trace corroborated 2.27s FCP/LCP on the faster unthrottled run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image, reduce render-blocking dependencies, subset fonts, and set a performance budget tested under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Images do not reserve intrinsic layout space.
findings.evidence: The images audit found all 14 images missing complete width/height dimensions; mobile CLS was 0.061 and showed many late shifts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height or aspect-ratio on every image and reserve stable space for banners, tickers and injected widgets.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JS and records long work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 293 KiB unused JavaScript; the trace recorded a 96.9ms long task and 46.9ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused libraries, load route-specific behavior only when needed and break remaining work into schedulable tasks.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is heavy and render-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 56 requests and 1.78MB transferred, including 384KB third-party fonts; seven parser-inserted stylesheets and synchronous scripts were confirmed by HAR and the DOM probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline critical CSS, defer non-critical assets, self-host/subset fonts, lazy-load below-fold images and provide responsive AVIF/WebP sources.

findings.summary: Most framework CSS and several libraries are unused on the landing route.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 179 KiB unused CSS and 293 KiB unused JS, including 99.9% of animate.min.css and 88.8% of fancybox.umd.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle per route, remove jQuery migration where no longer needed, and purge unused framework/icon styles.

findings.summary: Names, roles and labels are incomplete across key paths.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed dialog name, image alt and link name checks; the registration probe found 14 unlabeled controls and the images audit found two missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic controls, unique IDs, explicit labels, meaningful alternative text and accessible names for every dialog/link.

findings.summary: Document structure is malformed for assistive navigation.
findings.evidence: The home page has no doctype, lang, h1, main or nav; Lighthouse failed heading order and positive tabindex checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid doctype and language, one descriptive h1, semantic landmarks and DOM-order keyboard navigation without positive tabindex.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration restricts zoom and touch targets are too small.
findings.evidence: The viewport uses maximum-scale=1; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and the form probes found interactive targets only 19–23px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale/minimum-scale restrictions, verify 200–400% reflow, enlarge targets, and caption instructional media.

findings.summary: The entry document is in quirks mode and image markup omits intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no doctype and Lighthouse failed the doctype audit; the image audit found 14/14 images without complete intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit <!doctype html>, validate the rendered markup, and include width/height plus responsive sources for images.

findings.summary: The page disables user capabilities and relies on legacy synchronous libraries.
findings.evidence: The viewport caps zoom, Aadhaar fields block paste, and all seven external scripts are classic synchronous scripts without async/defer/module.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not block zoom or paste; modernise and defer scripts, and retain progressive fallbacks.

findings.summary: Every inspected route reuses a generic title and opaque description.
findings.evidence: Home, registration, tracking, about and privacy DOM captures all use “ई-विकास प्रणाली”; descriptions use the internal acronym “MP-FDCMS”.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each route a distinct descriptive title and a useful Hindi/English summary matching its task.

findings.summary: Many visible links are not crawlable and crawler-visible content coverage is low.
findings.evidence: The probe found visible anchors without href and href="#" placeholders; Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors. Raw HTML coverage was only 15%, despite not being an empty JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation, remove placeholder links, allow zoom, and ensure meaningful content is server-rendered.

findings.summary: Canonical, robots and sitemap signals are absent.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found no canonical or robots meta; /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml returned the site’s HTML 404 page rather than valid files.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid robots.txt and sitemap.xml, add self-referencing canonicals, and add hreflang if Hindi and English routes coexist.

findings.summary: The site provides no structured or social metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero JSON-LD scripts and zero Open Graph tags on the landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate GovernmentService/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata with stable titles, descriptions and images.

findings.summary: The CSP permits unsafe script execution and Permissions-Policy is absent.
findings.evidence: Headers include HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff, but CSP script-src allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; Permissions-Policy is missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Move inline code to nonce/hash-authorised scripts, remove unsafe-eval, and deploy a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Browser policy hardening is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The headers audit found no Permissions-Policy and a weakened CSP, although frame and referrer protections were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Harden CSP, add Permissions-Policy, and consider Trusted Types after removing legacy unsafe-eval dependencies.

findings.summary: Most rendered content is not represented as equivalent raw HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 15% overlap between rendered content words and raw HTML; crawler and rendered views differ materially.
findings.suggestedFix: Render primary service content and links in server HTML, then enhance behavior with JavaScript without replacing semantic content.

findings.summary: Failure and unavailable-service states do not offer recovery actions.
findings.evidence: The tracking path displays an unavailable-service paragraph without retry, status timestamp, or alternative action; requested robots/sitemap paths return generic framework 404 HTML.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide explicit offline/error states with retry, last-updated data and alternative contact/lookup routes.

findings.summary: Language declarations are missing or invalid across Hindi content.
findings.evidence: The Hindi home page has no lang attribute; inner routes declare lang="Eng", which is not a valid BCP 47 code and does not match the predominantly Hindi UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="hi" (or the correct BCP 47 value) per page/segment, use dir where needed and prefer logical CSS properties.

findings.summary: The forced notice and disabled paste reduce user control.
findings.evidence: The notice appears without user initiation and blocks the task; Aadhaar fields attach onpaste handlers returning false.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep notices non-blocking, preserve dismissal, and allow standard paste/password-manager/assistive input behavior.

findings.summary: Form constraints are enforced without accessible, humane feedback.
findings.evidence: The registration controls lack programmatic labels, duplicate IDs and block paste; the tracking state gives no actionable retry.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, connect specific errors with aria-describedby, announce summaries, preserve values and provide recovery.

findings.summary: The identity form disables useful input assistance.
findings.evidence: Aadhaar fields use autocomplete="off" and onpaste=false; several controls lack labels and duplicate IDs.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow paste, choose appropriate autocomplete/inputmode tokens, and make labels and instructions programmatically determinable.

findings.summary: Images are legacy, oversized and non-responsive.
findings.evidence: The images audit found 12 legacy-format assets, three oversized images, six without srcset and eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and srcset/sizes, right-size assets, lazy-load below-fold media and keep intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The route downloads substantial code and animation work that is not needed for the core task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 472 KiB combined unused CSS/JS, while the reduced-motion probe found perpetual animations still running.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused route code and stop decorative/background work when hidden or reduced motion is requested.

findings.summary: Fonts and media lack a disciplined transfer budget.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 1.78MB and 56 requests; 384KB came from third-party font origins and images transferred 581KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-route budgets, subset/self-host fonts, consolidate icon systems and defer non-critical media.
